title: Two Sum
description: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`. You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

examples.explanation: Because nums[0] + nums[1] == 9, we return [0, 1].

hints: A really brute force way would be to search for all possible pairs of numbers but that would be too slow.
Try using a hash map to store the complement.

title: Reverse String
description: Write a function that reverses a string. The input string is given as an array of characters `s`. You must do this by modifying the input array in-place with O(1) extra memory.
constraints: s[i] is a printable ascii character.
hints: The first approach that comes to mind is to use extra space.
Try swapping characters from both ends moving inward.

title: Valid Parentheses
description: Given a string `s` containing just the characters `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, `[` and `]`, determine if the input string is valid.
hints: Use a stack to keep track of opening brackets.
When you see a closing bracket, check if it matches the top of the stack.

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
description: You are given the heads of two sorted linked lists `list1` and `list2`. Merge the two lists into one sorted list.
constraints: The number of nodes in both lists is in the range [0, 50]
Both list1 and list2 are sorted in non-decreasing order.
hints: You can solve this recursively or iteratively.
Use a dummy head node to simplify edge cases.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
description: You are given an array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on the `ith` day. You want to maximize your profit by choosing a single day to buy one stock and choosing a different day in the future to sell that stock.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 2 (price = 1) and sell on day 5 (price = 6), profit = 6-1 = 5.
No transactions are done, max profit = 0.

hints: Think about tracking the minimum price seen so far.
For each price, calculate profit if sold at that price.

title: Maximum Subarray
description: Given an integer array `nums`, find the subarray with the largest sum, and return its sum.

examples.explanation: The subarray [4,-1,2,1] has the largest sum 6.

hints: Track current sum and max sum as you iterate.

title: Contains Duplicate
description: Given an integer array `nums`, return `true` if any value appears at least twice in the array, and return `false` if every element is distinct.
hints: Use a hash set to track seen elements.
Sort the array and check adjacent elements.

title: Palindrome Number
description: Given an integer `x`, return `true` if `x` is a palindrome. An integer is a palindrome when it reads the same backward as forward.

examples.explanation: From left to right, it reads -121. From right to left, it becomes 121-.

hints: Try reversing the number and comparing.

title: Fibonacci Number
description: The Fibonacci numbers, commonly denoted F(n), form a sequence called the Fibonacci sequence, such that each number is the sum of the two preceding ones, starting from 0 and 1.
hints: Start with the base cases: F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1.
Use iterative approach for O(n) time.

title: Power of Two
description: Given an integer n, return true if it is a power of two.
hints: A power of two in binary has exactly one 1 bit.

title: Linked List Cycle
description: Given head, the head of a linked list, determine if the linked list has a cycle in it.
constraints: The number of the nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4]
pos is -1 or a valid index in the linked-list.

examples.explanation: Tail connects to node at index 1.
Tail connects to node at index 0.
No cycle.

hints: Use Floyd's tortoise and hare algorithm.
Two pointers moving at different speeds will meet if there's a cycle.

title: Valid Anagram
description: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s, and false otherwise.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Missing Number
description: Given an array nums containing n distinct numbers in the range [0, n], return the only number in the range that is missing from the array.
constraints: All the numbers of nums are unique.

examples.explanation: n = 3 since there are 3 numbers, so all numbers are in the range [0,3]. 2 is the missing number.
n = 2, missing number is 2.
n = 9, missing number is 8.

title: Single Number
description: Given a non-empty array of integers nums, every element appears twice except for one. Find that single one.
constraints: Each element in the array appears twice except for one element which appears only once.

title: Majority Element
description: Given an array nums of size n, return the majority element.
hints: Sort and return the middle element.

title: Roman to Integer
description: Roman numerals are represented by seven different symbols: I, V, X, L, C, D, and M.
constraints: It is guaranteed that s is a valid roman numeral in the range [1, 3999].

examples.explanation: III = 3.

hints: Map each symbol to its value.
If a smaller value appears before a larger one, subtract it.

title: Climbing Stairs
description: You are climbing a staircase. It takes n steps to reach the top. Each time you can either climb 1 or 2 steps.

examples.explanation:
1. 1 step + 1 step
2. 2 steps

1. 1 step + 1 step + 1 step
2. 1 step + 2 steps
3. 2 steps + 1 step

hints: This is a Fibonacci sequence problem.

title: Valid Sudoku
description: Determine if a 9 x 9 Sudoku board is valid.
hints: Use hash sets for rows, columns, and 3x3 boxes.
Check each row, column, and box for duplicates.

title: Count and Say
description: The count-and-say sequence is a sequence of digit strings defined by the recursive formula.

examples.explanation:
countAndSay(1) = "1"
countAndSay(2) = "11"
countAndSay(3) = "21"
countAndSay(4) = "1211"

hints: Generate each sequence from the previous one.

title: Add Binary
description: Given two binary strings a and b, return their sum as a binary string.
constraints: a and b consist only of '0' or '1' characters.
Each string does not contain leading zeros except the zero itself.
hints: Use built-in int() to convert, add, then convert back.
Or implement manual binary addition with carry.

title: Length of Last Word
description: Given a string s consisting of words and spaces, return the length of the last word in the string.
constraints: s consists of only English letters and spaces.
There is at least one word in s.

examples.explanation: The last word is "World" with length 5.

examples.input: s = "   fly me   to   the moon  "
examples.explanation: The last word is "moon" with length 4.
The last word is "joyboy" with length 6.

hints: Return the length of the last element.

title: Plus One
description: You are given a large integer represented as an integer array digits. Increment the large integer by one and return the resulting array of digits.
constraints: digits does not contain any leading 0's.

title: Search Insert Position
description: Given a sorted array of distinct integers and a target value, return the index if the target is found.
constraints: All the integers in nums are unique.
nums is sorted in ascending order.

title: Binary Tree Inorder Traversal
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the inorder traversal of its nodes' values.
constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 100]
hints: Use recursion or an explicit stack.

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth.
constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 10^4]

title: Symmetric Tree
description: Given the root of a binary tree, check whether it is a mirror of itself (i.e., symmetric around its center).
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 1000]
hints: Compare left subtree with right subtree.

title: Convert Sorted Array to BST
description: Given an integer array nums where the elements are sorted in ascending order, convert it to a height-balanced binary search tree.
constraints: All the integers in nums are unique.
nums is sorted in ascending order.
hints: Pick the middle element as root.
Recursively build left and right subtrees.

title: Add Two Numbers
description: You are given two non-empty linked lists representing two non-negative integers.
constraints: The number of nodes in each linked list is in the range [1, 100]
It is guaranteed that the list represents a number that does not have leading zeros.
hints: Traverse both lists and add digit by digit with carry.
Use a dummy head to simplify list construction.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, symbols and spaces.

examples.explanation: The answer is "abc", with the length of 3.
The answer is "b", with the length of 1.
The answer is "wke", with the length of 3.

hints: Track characters in a set or map.

title: Container With Most Water
description: You are given an integer array height of length n. Find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container, such that the container contains the most water.
hints: Use two pointers from both ends.
Move the pointer with the smaller height.

title: 3Sum
description: Given an integer array nums, return all the triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i != j, i != k, and j != k, and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0.
hints: Fix one element and use two pointers for the rest.

title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
description: Given a string containing digits from 2-9 inclusive, return all possible letter combinations that the number could represent.
constraints: digits[i] is a digit in the range ['2', '9'].

title: Generate Parentheses
description: Given n pairs of parentheses, write a function to generate all combinations of well-formed parentheses.
hints: Only add '(' if count < n, only add ')' if count > open_count.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
description: There is an integer array nums sorted in ascending order (with distinct values).
constraints: All values of nums are unique.
nums is an ascending array that is possibly rotated.
hints: Determine which half is sorted, then search accordingly.

title: Combination Sum
description: Given an array of distinct integers candidates and a target integer target, return a list of all unique combinations.
constraints: All elements of candidates are distinct.
hints: Sort candidates to help with pruning.

title: Jump Game
description: You are given an integer array nums.

examples.explanation: Jump 1 step from index 0 to 1, then 3 steps to the last index.
You will always arrive at index 3 that has value 0.

hints: Greedy: update max_reach at each step.

title: Merge Intervals
description: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi], merge all overlapping intervals.
hints: Merge if current interval overlaps with the previous.

title: Group Anagrams
description: Given an array of strings strs, group the anagrams together.
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
hints: Sort each string to use as a key.
Use a hash map to group strings with the same sorted key.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements.
constraints: k is in the range [1, the number of unique elements in the array].
It is guaranteed that the answer is unique.
hints: Count frequencies, then use a heap or bucket sort.

title: Product of Array Except Self
description: Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] is equal to the product of all the elements of nums except nums[i].
constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix of nums is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit integer.
hints: Build two arrays: left products and right products.

title: Maximum Product Subarray
description: Given an integer array nums, find a subarray that has the largest product, and return the product.
constraints: The product of any subarray of nums is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: [2,3] has the largest product 6.

hints: Track both max and min products (negatives can flip).
At each position, the max is max(nums[i], max*nums[i], min*nums[i]).

title: Sort Colors
description: Given an array nums with n objects colored red, white, or blue, sort them in-place.

title: Decode Ways
description: A message containing letters from A-Z can be encoded into numbers using the mapping.
constraints: s consists only of digits and may contain leading zero(s).

examples.explanation: "12" can be decoded as "AB" (1 2) or "L" (12).
"226" can be decoded as "BZ" (2 26), "VF" (22 6), or "BBF" (2 2 6).
"06" cannot be mapped to "F" because "6" is different from "06".

hints: Check if single digit (1-9) and two digits (10-26) are valid.

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values.
constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 2000]

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
description: Given the root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST).
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 10^4]
hints: Use range validation: each node must be within (min, max).
Inorder traversal should be strictly increasing.

title: Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List
description: Given the root of a binary tree, flatten the tree into a 'linked list'.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 2000]

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
description: Given a binary tree, find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of two given nodes in the tree.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [2, 10^5]
p and q will exist in the tree.
hints: Recursively search left and right subtrees.
If both subtrees return non-null, current node is LCA.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
description: Given an unsorted array of integers nums, return the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence.

examples.explanation: The longest consecutive elements sequence is [1,2,3,4].

hints: Use a set for O(1) lookups.
Only start counting from the beginning of a sequence (num-1 not in set).

title: Clone Graph
description: Given a reference of a node in a connected undirected graph, return a deep copy of the graph.
constraints: The number of nodes in the graph is in the range [0, 100]
There are no repeated edges and no self-loops.
hints: Use DFS or BFS with a visited map.
Map original nodes to cloned nodes.

title: Number of Islands
description: Given an m x n 2D binary grid grid which represents a map of '1's (land) and '0's (water), return the number of islands.
hints: Use DFS/BFS to mark visited land.
Iterate through grid, start DFS when you find unvisited '1'.

title: Course Schedule
description: There are a total of numCourses courses you have to take.
hints: Detect cycles in the directed graph.
Use topological sort (BFS with in-degree or DFS).

title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
description: Implement a trie with insert, search, and startsWith methods.
constraints: word and prefix consist only of lowercase English letters.
At most 3 * 10^4 calls in total will be made to insert, search, and startsWith.
hints: Each node stores children as a map/array.
Mark end of word with a boolean.

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element in the array.
hints: Use a min-heap of size k.

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
description: Suppose an array of length n sorted in ascending order is rotated between 1 and n times.
constraints: All the integers of nums are unique.
nums is sorted and rotated between 1 and n times.
hints: Binary search for the pivot point.
The minimum is at the pivot.

title: Coin Change
description: You are given an integer array coins representing coins of different denominations and an integer amount.
hints: dp[i] = min coins needed for amount i.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
description: Given an integer array nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

examples.explanation: The longest increasing subsequence is [2,3,7,101].

hints: O(n^2) DP: dp[i] = length of LIS ending at i.
O(n log n): Use binary search with patience sorting.

title: Word Search
description: Given an m x n grid of characters board and a string word, return true if word exists in the grid.
constraints: board and word consists of only lowercase and uppercase English letters.
hints: Mark visited cells and unmark on backtrack.

title: LRU Cache
description: Design a data structure that follows the constraints of a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache.
constraints: At most 2 * 10^5 calls will be made to get and put.
hints: Combine a hash map with a doubly linked list.
Move accessed nodes to the front.

title: Trapping Rain Water
description: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
hints: Water at i = min(left_max, right_max) - height[i].

title: Merge k Sorted Lists
description: You are given an array of k linked-lists lists, each linked-list is sorted in ascending order.
constraints: lists[i] is sorted in ascending order.
The total number of nodes across all lists is in the range [0, 10^4].
hints: Or divide and conquer: merge pairs of lists.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
description: Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2 of size m and n respectively, return the median of the two sorted arrays.

examples.explanation: merged array = [1,2,3] and median is 2.
merged array = [1,2,3,4] and median is (2+3)/2 = 2.5.

hints: Binary search on the shorter array.
Partition both arrays so left half has same total elements.

title: Regular Expression Matching
description: Given an input string s and a pattern p, implement regular expression matching with support for '.' and '*'.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters.
p contains only lowercase English letters, '.', and '*'.
It is guaranteed for each appearance of the character '*', there will be a previous valid character to match.

examples.explanation: '*' means zero or more of 'a'.

hints: Handle '*' by considering 0 or more occurrences.

title: Longest Valid Parentheses
description: Given a string containing just the characters '(' and ')', find the length of the longest valid (well-formed) parentheses substring.

examples.explanation: The longest valid parentheses substring is '()'
The longest valid parentheses substring is '()'
The longest valid parentheses substring is '(())'

hints: Use a stack to track indices.
Or use DP: dp[i] = length of longest valid ending at i.

title: N-Queens
description: The n-queens puzzle is the problem of placing n queens on an n x n chessboard such that no two queens attack each other.
hints: Use sets to track occupied columns and diagonals.

title: Word Ladder
description: A transformation sequence begins with beginWord, endWord, and a wordList.
constraints: beginWord, endWord, and wordList[i] consist of lowercase English letters.
All the words in wordList are unique.

examples.explanation: hit -> hot -> dot -> dog -> cog

hints: Use BFS to find shortest path.
Pre-process word patterns for efficient neighbor lookup.

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
description: A path in a binary tree is a sequence of nodes where each pair of adjacent nodes in the sequence has an edge connecting them.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 3 * 10^4]
hints: At each node, update global max with left + node + right.

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
description: Design an algorithm to serialize and deserialize a binary tree.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 10^4]
hints: Use pre-order traversal with null markers.
Split the serialized string to reconstruct.

title: Edit Distance
description: Given two strings word1 and word2, return the minimum number of operations required to convert word1 to word2.
constraints: word1 and word2 consist of lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: r->h, h->o, e->r (replace h->o, replace r->s, delete e)

hints: 2D DP: dp[i][j] = min operations to convert word1[0..i] to word2[0..j].
If chars match, dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]. Else consider insert/delete/replace.

title: Climbing Stairs II
description: You are climbing a staircase with n steps. Each time you can climb 1, 2, or 3 steps.

examples.explanation: Climb step 2 (cost 15).
Climb steps 1,3,5,7,9.

hints: dp[i] = min cost to reach step i.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
description: You are given an array of integers nums, there is a sliding window of size k which is moving from the very left of the array to the very right.
hints: Remove elements outside the window and smaller elements.

title: Find Median from Data Stream
description: The median is the middle value in an ordered integer list.
constraints: There will be at least one element in the data structure before calling findMedian.
At most 5 * 10^4 calls will be made to addNum and findMedian.
hints: Use two heaps: max-heap for lower half, min-heap for upper half.
Balance the heaps so their sizes differ by at most 1.

title: Alien Dictionary
description: Given a sorted list of words in an alien language, find the order of characters in that language.
constraints: words[i] consists of only lowercase English letters.
hints: Compare adjacent words to find character order.
Build a graph and perform topological sort.

title: Russian Doll Envelopes
description: You are given a 2D array of integers envelopes where envelopes[i] = [wi, hi].
hints: Sort by width, then find LIS on heights.
To handle equal widths, sort by height descending.
